newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Riksbank cuts key repo rate for 19th time.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Riksbank cuts key repo rate for 19th time.

text.p: Sweden's central bank, the Riksbank, on Tuesday cut its repo rate for the 19th time this year, trimming a further 10 basis points at its regular weekly tender to take this key interest rate down to 5.15 percent.
The move was widely expected by the financial markets with 14 of 18 analysts questioned by Reuters on Monday forecasting a cut of 15 basis points and the other four forecasting a 10 basis points cut.
The repo rate is the Riksbank's key tool for controlling money market liquidity and is the central rate in its three tier system.
Since the start of the year the repo rate has been lowered from 8.91 percent with the Riksbank saying low inflation has given room for the downward moves.
The repo rate was last lowered on August 27 when it was trimmed by 15 basis points.
The other two elements of the Riksbank's interest rate corridor, the deposit and lending rates, are currently set at 4.75 percent and 6.25 percent respectively.
The Riksbank last lowered its interest rate corridor on August 15.
Analysts forecast the repo rate would be lowered further in coming weeks with an average forecast for the rate to bottom at 4.68 percent this autumn.
The outlook for lower rates was backed at the weekend when Riksbank governor Urban Backstrom said there was more room for monetary easing even though inflation is likely to rise in the autumn.
Speaking at country's trade union federation (LO) annual conference, Backstrom said: "I still believe there is room for further easing of monetary policy."
He said the bank's inflation report on September 24 would shed some light on the extent to which rates could be further lowered.
